question: Would randomising at the store-category level let us test the shallower ladder on bakery and dairy in one experiment?

transcript.content: Would randomising at the store-category level let us test the shallower ladder on bakery and dairy in one experiment?

content.text:
Yes, randomising at the store-category level would let you test the shallower ladder on bakery and dairy in one experiment.

At store-category granularity, each store contributes two independent units to the randomisation—one for bakery and one for dairy. This means you could assign some store-category pairs to the treatment (shallow_ladder_policy@v1) and others to the control (ladder_policy@v1), all within the same experiment.

The key advantage is that within a single store, bakery might be in the treatment arm while dairy is in the control arm (or vice versa), or both could be assigned the same way. This gives you independent randomisation at the store-category level, which should avoid interference between the two categories within the same store, since they have separate supply chains and pricing levers.

This design would be more efficient than running two separate store-level experiments—you'd get roughly twice the statistical power for the same number of stores, because you're using the store-category variation rather than treating each entire store as a monolith.
